job_description_info.job_description:
# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

Dear Tejo Insurance Tech recruitment team,

I would like to apply for the Backend Engineer (Java) position.

At Viajar Online I have spent over two years working on the booking and payments parts of a large Java application. I enjoy the moment when a slow, fragile part of a system becomes predictable, and I have done this several times, most visibly when I raised test coverage of the payments module from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, which let us refactor it safely.

I was also part of the small group that started splitting our monolith. I extracted the notifications service into its own Spring Boot application, which taught me a lot about messaging, retries and the operational side of running separate services.

Insurance is new to me as a domain, but quoting and claims share many patterns with booking and payments: many partners, many rules, and a strong need for correctness. I am excited about the chance to work with Kafka and Kubernetes in production.

Thank you for considering my application.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Its products help customers plan routes and loads, book carriers, track shipments in real time, and manage delivery and customs documents. More than 340 forwarders across 19 countries use its platform, which processes tens of millions of shipment events daily.

The company’s work focuses on making freight operations more efficient and transparent—reducing manual status chasing and helping dispatchers and their customers see where shipments are. Tessel is growing its live-tracking capabilities and investing in the reliability and scalability of its services.

Its stated values are **“Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.”** The engineering culture emphasizes small teams, ownership of the services they build and operate, clear communication, concise design notes, and dedicated time for reliability work. Teams work across Antwerp, Poznań, and a remote-first engineering group; engineers are expected to take part in on-call operations and enjoy running production systems.

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.
# Careers at Tessel Cargo Software
*(fictional careers page – tesselcargo.example/careers)*

## Build the software behind Europe's supply chains

**Engineering at Tessel**
- Stack: Python (FastAPI), Go for a few high-throughput workers, PostgreSQL, Kafka, AWS (EKS, RDS, S3), Terraform, GitHub Actions, Grafana/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry
- Team structure: product teams of 6-8 engineers with an engineering manager and a product manager
- Practices: trunk-based development, code review within one working day, blameless post-mortems, one week in six on call (with a rota bonus)
- We publish our architectural decisions as short ADRs and invite candidates to read two of them before the interview.

**Benefits:** hybrid work, EUR 1,500 learning budget, 28 days holiday, pension scheme, home-office allowance, company-paid language lessons.

**Hiring process:** intro call (30 min) -> technical conversation about a past project (60 min) -> system-design discussion (60 min) -> meeting with the team and engineering manager. No take-home tests.

**What we look for:** people who have run software in production, communicate clearly in writing, and like understanding the business problem behind a ticket. Logistics experience is a bonus, not a requirement.

generated_cover_letter:
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on the Routing & Tracking team. I bring more than seven years of backend development experience building and operating services, primarily with Java and Kotlin, and I am interested in applying that experience in a role focused mainly on Python. Tessel’s focus on dependable, scalable tracking services is a strong match for the systems I have worked on.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I design and maintain Spring Boot services using PostgreSQL, Kafka and Kubernetes. I designed a versioned REST API for broker partners that now supports around 400,000 quote requests per month. I also resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox pattern and idempotency keys; duplicates fell from about 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These projects have strengthened my focus on API reliability, data correctness and clear technical trade-offs.

I take part in a monthly on-call rota and handled a major Kafka lag incident, documenting the follow-up in a post-incident account. I also have experience with Docker, AWS services including EKS, S3 and SQS, and automated testing with Testcontainers and contract tests. My professional backend work has been in Java and Kotlin; my Python experience is limited to data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and I have not yet shipped a Python service. I am keen to build on my production experience while developing further in Python.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in backend services, event-driven systems and production reliability could contribute to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment tracking platform.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

I am keen to build on my production experience while developing further in Python.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience in backend services, event-driven systems and production reliability could contribute to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment tracking platform.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a concise, professional cover letter with a clear structure: application motivation, relevant production experience, reliability/on-call experience, and a transparent explanation of the candidate's limited Python background. The quantified API volume and reduction in duplicate claims provide credible evidence of impact. The letter also explains technical trade-offs clearly, which matches an explicit requirement. Its main weakness is that it spends substantial space emphasizing what the candidate has not done in Python rather than positioning Java/Kotlin as the comparable backend experience accepted by the advertisement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard paragraph formatting, no tables or graphics, and includes relevant searchable terms such as Python, Java, Kotlin, backend services, REST API, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Docker, AWS, EKS, S3, SQS, Testcontainers, contract tests, and on-call. AI screening probability is good for the comparable-language route and for event-driven backend reliability. Screening strength is reduced because the letter does not contain evidence for query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, or FastAPI; these should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information. The wording is otherwise parseable and appropriately keyword-rich without apparent keyword stuffing.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's comparable-language allowance: the candidate has more than seven years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience, REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS/Kubernetes exposure, automated testing, Kafka, production on-call experience, and English-language work. The quantified API and Kafka reliability examples also fit the team's focus on dependable, scalable tracking services and event-driven systems. The candidate's material does not establish professional Python service development, query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD ownership, observability tooling, logistics or EDI experience, Dutch/French skills, or Terraform module development. These are candidate-profile gaps or unverified areas rather than defects that can be repaired through wording. The letter appropriately avoids claiming them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR IMPROVEMENT 1 — In the opening paragraph, replace "I am interested in applying that experience in a role focused mainly on Python" with a more direct statement that mirrors the job's comparable-language requirement while remaining truthful, for example: "I bring more than seven years of professional backend experience in Java and Kotlin, comparable production languages for this role, and I am ready to work mainly in Python." This makes the qualification and willingness explicit earlier without implying unearned Python service experience.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT 2 — In the third paragraph, replace "I also have experience with Docker, AWS services including EKS, S3 and SQS, and automated testing with Testcontainers and contract tests" with "I have production experience using Docker and AWS services including EKS, S3 and SQS, alongside automated testing with Testcontainers and contract testing." This uses the advertisement's terms more closely and clarifies the candidate's truthful level of AWS experience without claiming infrastructure-as-code ownership.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT 3 — In the closing paragraph, change "could contribute to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment tracking platform" to "could contribute to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment tracking platform through reliable REST services, event-driven systems and production operations." This connects the candidate's demonstrated experience more directly to the role while avoiding unsupported claims about logistics or shipment tracking.
